text:
samir khan: Hey all — first week dev env weirdness. I `docker compose up` and my app tries to connect to postgres over a unix socket (socket path /var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432) and crashes. I expected it to talk to service `postgres:5432`. I'm on mac, running the api container.

samir khan: compose snippet (redacted):
```yaml
services:
  api:
    build: .
    env_file: .env.dev
    depends_on: [postgres]
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    volumes:
      - ./dev/pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

samir khan: my .env.dev has DATABASE_URL=postgresql:///app (no host). Not sure where that came from.

olivia ng: welcome samir! that DATABASE_URL (postgresql:///app) means use a unix socket on the default socket dir. inside a container that resolves to a socket path inside the api container, not the postgres container. if you want TCP to postgres service, set host in the URL: `postgres://postgres:pass@postgres:5432/app_dev`.

matt rao: also note env_file variables are loaded into the container env but can be overridden by actual env or compose `environment:`. `docker compose config` prints the resolved env so you can verify which DATABASE_URL is active.

samir khan: ahhh I forgot we had a legacy .env.dev example. I changed it to `postgres://postgres:password@postgres:5432/app_dev` and re-built. still fails though — logs show `could not connect to server: Connection refused` and `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:5432` in the stack.

olivia ng: are you exec'ing into the api container or running the app on host? 127.0.0.1 suggests either the app still uses a fallback, or the containerized app is trying localhost. Run `docker compose exec api env | grep DATABASE_URL` and `docker compose exec api ping -c1 postgres` to test name resolution.

samir khan: ran those: env inside container shows the correct postgres URL. `ping postgres` works. but the app binary inside the container logs 127.0.0.1.

matt rao: sometimes frameworks read a different config file at runtime or prefer a socket when host omitted. Could be your app parses DATABASE_URL differently. Try `docker compose exec api sh -c 'printenv DATABASE_URL; cat /app/config/runtime.yml'` (or whatever file) to see the runtime config. Also make sure the binary was rebuilt after env change — if you're mounting source and the compiled binary was built locally, it might be stale.

samir khan: oof I had mounted `./target:/app/target` from host and the binary was stale (built on host). Rebuilding inside container fixed it. Now app connects to postgres:5432.

olivia ng: nice! small extra: avoid mounting compiled artifacts from host on mac (permission + arch) — prefer using mounted source only and run `cargo build` in container or use docker named volume for target.

matt rao: and if you ever need to reach postgres from host (not container), map the port `ports: - "5432:5432"` but be mindful of collisions with host postgres. For dev, we usually skip ports and rely on service name to avoid that.

samir khan: one more curious thing: my host `./dev/pg` dir got owned by root after postgres created files. How do folks reset that safely?

olivia ng: stop compose, then run `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) dev/pg` if you need host access. If you just want to nuke it, `rm -rf dev/pg` and let postgres recreate it. For preserving data, use `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/dev/pg:/data alpine chown -R 999:999 /data`.

devex-bot: Tip: onboarding doc updated with 'avoid mounting build artifacts' and example `docker-compose.override.yml`. See /devenv/compose-local for snippet.

samir khan: thanks everyone — up and running and adding a note to the README about the old .env.dev example. Appreciate the quick help! :clap:
